q7.answer: I did not design a notification mechanism. The document only says billing_mode lives in the config service, workers keep the last known mode if it is unreachable, and the idempotency key stops double charges if workers briefly disagree. How workers learn of a change (poll or push) and what happens to an in-flight invoice at that moment is not specified.

q8.answer: Gate evidence (gate counters, Finance sign-off, mode entry time) is kept in the rollout controller's own durable record outside the flag, which I flagged as an assumption to confirm. Only the controller writes billing_mode, and it rejects any skipped step or any move whose gate is not met.

q9.answer: I did not name a specific detecting component. The rule is that when the new engine's charge failure rate exceeds 2% over any 10-minute window in both or new_only (while still reversible), an automatic rollback starts. The rollout controller is the program that runs rollback, but which component does the measuring was not decided.

q10.answer: At freeze, both engines stop issuing charges and charges that fall due are queued, not dropped. They are made at the hand-off step, when the old engine charges only periods that are due and not already charged, including the queued ones, before the flip to old_only.

q11.answer: Reconcile matches the ledger to the payment provider so every (customer, billing period) is known as charged or not. At hand-off the old engine charges only unpaid periods, and every charge carries the idempotency key (customer, billing period), checked against the ledger and the payment provider, which refuse a repeat.

q12.answer: The rollout goes to rollback_stalled after retries are exhausted and on-call is paged. Charging stays frozen, so charges are delayed but never dropped or doubled, and billing_mode is not yet flipped. Once on-call fixes the cause, the rollback resumes at the failed step, since each step is safe to repeat.
